column11: Why does hepatic steatosis lose signal on opposed-phase GRE MRI?
column12: Normal liver voxels may contain both water and fat protons. On in-phase images their signals add; on opposed-phase images the fat and water components are out of phase and partially cancel, so voxels containing intracellular fat lose signal. This directly explains why opposed-phase signal dropout confirms hepatic steatosis.
